what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1989?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 2010 report (calendar wages) and FY2011-FY2025 (fiscal). The 1989 annual town report (84 pages) prints no wage list: its text was searched for wage, gross, payroll, earning, salary and compensation and returned only the balance sheet's ACCRUED WAGES PAYABLE (p26), appropriation lines for salaries (pp29-35, p52-53) and the Article 6 vote on the salary plan (p51) -- no list by employee (sources/data/report-tables/1989/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1989 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in fiscal 1990?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1989 annual town report records the vote but not the schedule: Article 6 of the May 13, 1989 Annual Town Meeting replaced `the Classification and Salary Schedule voted on May 14, 1988` with the one `proposed by the Personnel Committee and appearing in the Report of the Finance Committee`, effective July 1, 1989 -- VOTED UNANIMOUSLY (p51). The text was searched for salary schedule, classification, step and grade and returned only that article (sources/data/report-tables/1989/). — closes: the Finance Committee's report to the May 13, 1989 Annual Town Meeting (the schedule it printed).

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in fiscal 1989?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1989 annual town report prints no special revenue schedule: the only special revenue figures are the balance sheet's SPECIAL REVENUE column ($165,972 of cash and $164,705 total fund equity, p26). The text was searched for special revenue, revolving and grant and returned department prose and the trust accounts' GRANTS & GIFTS column (pp42-44); gift and grant articles appear as rows INSIDE the general fund schedule (e.g. `Town Record Gift Fund`, p30) (sources/data/report-tables/1989/). — closes: the Town Accountant's fiscal 1989 special revenue fund ledger.

what: What was appropriated, spent and carried forward on each capital project fund in fiscal 1989?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds a separate capital project fund schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1989 annual town report prints none; its balance sheet carries a CAPITAL PROJECTS column with $41,175 of cash and the same equity (p26), and capital articles appear inside the general fund appropriations schedule (pp29-35). Searched for capital project, capital fund and capital plan; only the `Capital Planning` account (p29) and a committee charge (p25) returned (sources/data/report-tables/1989/). — closes: the Town Accountant's fiscal 1989 capital projects fund ledger.

what: How much of Lunenburg's debt at the end of 1989 sat inside the debt limit, and how much outside it?
why: The inside/outside-the-limit split of 2001-2010 is not in the 1989 report. Its debt pages (p39-p40) mark only INTEREST (EXEMPTED) on the two elementary school remodelling issues and the ambulance (p40); the text was searched for `debt limit`, `inside` and `exempt` and returned nothing else (sources/data/report-tables/1989/). — closes: the Treasurer's debt statement for 1989, or the Town's Schedule A filed with the Department of Revenue.

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for fiscal 1989?
why: `report-valuation` holds the Assessors' valuation table from later reports. The 1989 report prints only the two valuation totals on its first page (`$572,393,407-Real Estate`, `$10,664,300-Personal Prop.`, p3) and a TAX RATE of $10.27; the text was searched for valuation, overlay, levy and new growth and returned prose about the 1990 revaluation (pp7-8) and the Assessors' exemption table (p8) (sources/data/report-tables/1989/). The p3 tax rate carries no year. — closes: the Assessors' fiscal 1989 tax rate recapitulation (LA-5) filed with the Department of Revenue.
